title: Multiple positive solutions to a perturbed Gelfand problem involving mixed local-nonlocal operators and singular nonlinearity: the Hopf-type strong comparison principle (Lemma 6.4)
author: Sarbani Pramanik
work: Multiple positive solutions to a perturbed Gelfand problem involving mixed local-nonlocal operators and singular nonlinearity
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma 6.4 (source0.tex lines 712-714, printed as Lemma 6.4 on page 14 of the published version), the Hopf-type Strong Comparison Principle for the singular mixed local-nonlocal operator in the remaining range s in [1/2,1): if two positive C^{1,alpha} functions solve the singular system with ordered right-hand sides, then u_1 < u_2 inside and the normal derivatives are strictly ordered at the boundary. The retained complete proof (lines 716-765) is a genuine 50-line boundary estimate, not a routine verification: it must control the fractional Laplacian of the barrier function near the boundary by estimating the Hessian through the distance function, split the nonlocal integral into an inner and an outer part, treat the endpoint case s = 1/2 separately by a large-ball truncation argument built on the article's C^{1,alpha} extension lemma, and then choose the exponent gamma so that the two competing powers of the distance beat each other before applying the weak comparison principle. The article itself states in its concluding remark that the main difficulty in obtaining the third solution is proving this Hopf-type Strong Comparison Principle for the nonlinear mixed operator, which is research-level nonlinear analysis far beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
